date.source: The post's own Usenet dateline and its own text ('the results from the final round').

evidence.source: The federation's own results post, subject 'NEWCOWF TOURNAMENT FINALS RESULTS' (8 June 1997)
evidence.note: Full announcer-narrated results for three championship finals plus two bonus matches; the sole and primary source for this record.

matches.title: newcowf-1997-tv
matches.stipulation: Tournament final, for the vacant NEWCOWF TV Title
matches.note: Ahmed Johnson dominated most of the offense, but Ric Flair answered a sidewalk slam attempt with a crotch shot, a knee clip and the figure-four for the pin at 21:37, becoming the first NEWCOWF TV Champion. Votes 6-4.

matches.stipulation: Bonus match, special referee Taz (not registered as a match participant)
matches.note: Vader powerbombed Ken Shamrock four times; special referee Taz declared Shamrock the winner at 17:23 after Vader shoved him, then Taz choked out both Vader and the refusing Shamrock with the Tazmission, leaving both unconscious. Votes 6-1 (with 3 for Taz). No clear result stands.

matches.title: newcowf-1997-tag-team
matches.stipulation: Tournament final, for the vacant NEWCOWF Tag Team Title
matches.note: John Kronus wrestled most of the match alone against both Furnas and LaFon while an injured Perry Saturn waited on the apron; Saturn tagged in at the ten-minute mark and hit an enziguri with his own leg cast for the pin at 13:42. The debuting Eliminators became the first NEWCOWF Tag Team Champions. Votes 7-2.

Sting cleared the ring of the Hart Foundation with a baseball bat, but Bret Hart clipped his knee with a chair and applied the Sharpshooter; the referee stopped the match at 27:02 after Sting passed out from the pain. Votes 4-3.

matches.title: newcowf-1997-world
matches.stipulation: Tournament final, for the vacant NEWCOWF World Title
matches.note: The Giant chokeslammed Steve Austin, who kicked out at two, low-blowed the Giant and delivered three consecutive Stone Cold Stunners for the pin at 11:24, becoming the first NEWCOWF World Champion. Votes 7-2. A post-match angle followed: Bret Hart interrupted on the video wall, then attacked Austin with a chair before Sting ran in with his bat; Austin turned the bat on Sting and hit another Stone Cold Stunner to close the show.

name: NEWCOWF Triple Threat '97

date.source: The results post's own Usenet dateline (29 June 1997), with a same-day follow-up post supplying the card's final two matches.

evidence.source: The federation's own results post, subject 'NEWCOWF TRIPLE THREAT'97 RESULTS' (29 June 1997), with a same-day follow-up, 'NEWCOWF TRIPLE THREAT'97 RESULTS PART 2', supplying the Street Fight and World Title results left off the first post.
evidence.note: Full announcer-narrated results for an eight-match card, including the promotion's first NEWCOWF TV and Tag Team Title changes.

matches.title: newcowf-1997-tv
matches.note: Back-and-forth mat wrestling for about fifteen minutes; Ric Flair worked over Chris Benoit's leg and went for the figure-four twice, but Benoit twice reached the ropes and then hit a top rope headbutt for the pin at 21:02, becoming the new NEWCOWF TV Champion. Votes 10-5.

matches.title: newcowf-1997-tag-team
matches.stipulation: For the NEWCOWF Tag Team Title; Tommy Dreamer substituted for an injured Perry Saturn, defending alongside champion John Kronus
matches.note: Kronus and Sabu traded high spots in the ring for over fifteen minutes while Dreamer and Van Dam brawled outside; Jerry Lawler ran in on Van Dam's side and was caned off by the Sandman, and Sabu put Kronus through a table. Dreamer hit a DDT on Van Dam, but with the referee distracted the Insane Clown Posse beat Dreamer down with 2-liter Faygo bottles; Van Dam finished him with a split-legged moonsault at 22:13 for the pin. Sabu and Rob Van Dam became the new NEWCOWF Tag Team Champions. Votes 12-3.

Vader wore Ken Shamrock down early with corner strikes; Taz made Vader tap to the Tazmission at 17:23, then traded suplexes with Shamrock for several minutes before tapping himself to a torque leglock at 24:21, leaving Shamrock the last man standing. Votes Shamrock 9, Taz 5, Vader 1.

matches.title: newcowf-1997-world
matches.stipulation: Triple-threat match for the NEWCOWF World Title
matches.note: Austin and Hart brawled into the crowd while Sting stood ready with his bat; Sting hit Hart with the Scorpion Death Drop and applied the Scorpion Death Lock, but Austin recovered to pin Sting with a Stone Cold Stunner at 21:02. Hart then battered Austin's knee with the bat and held the Sharpshooter for seven minutes before Austin broke free and hit a second Stone Cold Stunner out of nowhere for the pin at 37:15, retaining the title. Votes Austin 8, Hart 3, Sting 4.

notes: Undercard, not structured above: the Sandman beat Chris Jericho in the opener; Harlem Heat won a three-way brawl over the Gangstas and the Public Enemy for a future Tag Team Title shot; Cactus Jack beat Terry Funk in a barbed wire weapons match; and a Street Fight pitted the New World Order (Kevin Nash, Scott Hall, Syxx and Randy Savage) against the Nation of Domination (Farooq, D-Lo Brown and Kama Mustafa, with Ahmed Johnson sidelined by a storyline knee injury) and the Hart Foundation (Owen Hart, British Bulldog, Brian Pillman and Jim Neidhart), won by the New World Order.

name: NEWCOWF Clash in the Champions House

date.source: The results post's own Usenet dateline and its own text (results as previewed for the 13 July 1997 card).

evidence.source: The federation's own results post, subject 'NEWCOWF CLASH IN THE CHAMPIONS HOUSE RESULTS' (13 July 1997).
evidence.note: Full announcer-narrated results for a five-match card, including a NEWCOWF TV Title change and a NEWCOWF Tag Team Title defense.

matches.title: newcowf-1997-tag-team
matches.stipulation: For the NEWCOWF Tag Team Title
matches.note: Booker T had Rob Van Dam set up for the Harlem Hangover when the Insane Clown Posse ran in and pushed him off the top rope; Sabu followed with a moonsault for the pin at 29:17. Sabu and Rob Van Dam retained the title. Votes 7-6.

matches.title: newcowf-1997-tv
matches.note: Nearly 29 minutes of back-and-forth mat wrestling; Chris Benoit superplexed Ken Shamrock and went up for a top rope headbutt but missed with ten seconds left, and Shamrock hit a belly-to-belly suplex for the pin at 29:58 to win the title. Votes 7-6.

notes: Undercard, not structured above: the Sandman and Tommy Dreamer beat the Insane Clown Posse in the opener; the Public Enemy beat the Gangstas in a bloody street fight; and Steve Austin retained the NEWCOWF World Title by pinning Cactus Jack in a brutal brawl at 31:15.

name: NEWCOWF Great Canadian Bash

date.source: The federation's own vote card, naming the event 'NEWCOWF PRESENTS GREAT CANADIAN BASH 97-AUGUST 24, 1997-CALGARY, AB' (posted 10 August 1997); its own short results post followed on 25 August 1997.

evidence.source: The federation's own short results post, subject 'NEWCOWF GREAT CANADIAN BASH SHORT RESULTS' (25 August 1997), cross-read against its own vote card (10 August 1997) for the pre-card billing.
evidence.note: List-form results only (the operator's own post explains detailed results now go out by mailing list); confirms the NEWCOWF TV Title already back on Chris Benoit and the NEWCOWF Tag Team Title held up after a four-way draw.

matches.title: newcowf-1997-tv
matches.note: Chris Benoit beat Owen Hart by submission in 34:21 to retain the NEWCOWF TV Title -- the promotion's own vote card (10 August 1997) already billed Benoit as champion, the title having returned to him from Ken Shamrock off-page since Clash in the Champions House. Votes 9-4.

matches.title: newcowf-1997-world
matches.stipulation: For the NEWCOWF World Title, with the entire Hart family caged at ringside
matches.note: Steve Austin pinned Bret Hart in 37:12 to retain the NEWCOWF World Title, with the entire Hart family locked in a cage at ringside. Votes 10-3.

notes: A four-way for the NEWCOWF Tag Team Title among champions Sabu and Rob Van Dam, the Insane Clown Posse, Harlem Heat, and the Sandman and Tommy Dreamer ended in a double-pin draw between Harlem Heat and the champions at 24:37; the title was held up (not structured above -- two of the four sides are not otherwise on this wing's record). Elsewhere on the card: the Sandman beat Terry Funk and Cactus Jack beat Headhunter 1 in the first round of a NEWCOWF Death Match Title tournament (a fourth title, never crowned in the held record); the Undertaker beat the Giant; the Public Enemy beat Raven and Stevie Richards; Ken Shamrock beat Chris "Tatanka" Chavis by submission in 47 seconds; and Kevin Nash, Scott Hall and Syxx beat Hulk Hogan, Randy Savage and Dennis Rodman.

name: NEWCOWF Halloween Hangover 97

date.source: The post's own Usenet dateline (12 October 1997); the card itself is billed for 2 November 1997 in New Orleans, LA.

evidence.source: The federation's own vote card, subject '[VOTE]NEWCOWF HALLOWEEN HANGOVER 97' (12 October 1997) -- the fed's own last surviving post in the held record.
evidence.note: A pairings announcement only, dedicated to the memory of Brian Pillman; no results survive for this card in the held record.

notes: The federation's own last surviving post in the held record: a pairings announcement for a 2 November 1997 card in New Orleans, dedicated to the memory of Brian Pillman (1962-1997). Billed challengers for the semi-finals of the fed's own Death Match Title tournament (the Sandman vs. Cactus Jack, Tommy Dreamer vs. Sabu) and several other undercard bouts are named without any structured result; no further post survives in the held record and no closure notice is given.
